findings.summary: The executor reports a fatal NUL check before the shim runs. All three real Engine cases returned ConnectTimeout.
findings.child_stderr: [FATAL:electron\shell\common\node_bindings.cc:735] Unable to open nul device needed for initialization,aborting startup. As a workaround, try starting with --no-stdio-init
findings.mechanism: Hypothesis consistent with documented WRITE_RESTRICTED semantics and Electron IsNulDeviceEnabled; device ACL and effective token were not independently supplied as reproducible evidence.
findings.negative_control: restricted child: `echo x>nul && echo allowed>profile\allowed.txt` leaves allowed.txt absent
findings.positive_control: unrestricted token, same shell and line: exit 0 and the file is created
findings.not_reproduced_by: stdio validity - the abort persists when all three std handles are real files rather than NUL handles
findings.rejected_workaround: The executor reports ConnectTimeout with --no-stdio-init. Its exact effect on inherited stdin was not measured independently; no production flag change is accepted.

findings.summary: The restricted-token ACL negative control never executed: its argv[0] was built as System32/cmd.exe with a forward slash, which cmd.exe reads as a switch and rejects with `The syntax of the command is incorrect.` before any access check.
The same probe passed cmd.exe a command string quoted for CommandLineToArgvW; cmd.exe /S strips only the outer quote pair, so the CRT backslash escape landed inside the redirection target.
The probe asserted the profile file contains `allowed\r\n` while the command line put a space before `&`, which cmd.exe echoes, so the assertion could not have held even with a valid command line.
The handoff clone command is --single-branch, so neither origin/main nor main resolves and cargo xtask parity-check fails on the v4 overlay diff target rather than on ledger content.
findings.workaround_used: git fetch origin main:refs/remotes/origin/main, which adds a read-only remote ref and moves neither HEAD nor the branch
